bundle: WI-8 — Industrials real-issuer validation (KEC International Limited)
scope: IRR only; no IPD writes, no policy change, no new persistence mechanism, no validator change

sectorRationale: Industrials declares DCF_FCFF (PRIMARY), EV_EBITDA (SECONDARY) and EV_REVENUE (CROSS_CHECK with mandatory IN_BOOK_TO_BILL) and no PE_RELATIVE, so it exercises the enterprise-value family end to end.

It was the next sector in the roadmap after Technology, Consumer, and the Technology re-validations; selecting it required an issuer with a print-level debt decomposition and an order book, which is a harder bar than Consumer's.
issuerRationale: Three consecutive audited consolidated periods are printed in two documents: FY2025-26 report (FY2026 and FY2025 columns) and FY2024-25 report (FY2024 comparative column).

Note 30 decomposes current borrowings into demand loans, other short-term borrowings, financial-institution commercial paper and current maturities, so the governed gross-debt sum can be built without inference.

The consolidated statements carry no non-controlling interest and no preference capital line, and the balance sheet has no current-investments line: a genuine D-2 test in which absence must stay unavailable.
The auditor is a Big Four firm, the framework is Ind AS, and the statements are signed, so period eligibility and taxonomy compatibility are not in question.

boundary: WI-8 extends the programme's fourth shape of D-2 discipline: a filing that is fully read, fully audited and perfectly legible can supply every component the debt side needs and still fail the cash side — and the correct answer is a published refusal plus a named blocking component, not a substituted zero.
